findings_not_failures.lane: SMB-PS-GRADIENT-BUCKET-1 (lead note c, tolerance and dither)
findings_not_failures.finding: A gradient rewrites pixels it does not visibly paint. With no selection, pigment's coverage is u16::MAX for every pixel of the fill bounds (pigment fill_tools.rs:629), so masked_replace replaces every pixel there. commit_fill decodes the whole result (harness-view fill_tools.rs:461) after the layer was encoded through Prism's moncurve sRGB (prism view_transform.rs:266/956, linear slope ~12.923 below ~0.00304), while the viewer's decode is the IEC curve (fill_tools.rs:176-178, 12.92 below 0.04045). Where the paint alpha is 0 (past the end of the default foreground-to-transparent drag) the pixel comes back changed: values above 1 are clamped to 1, and linear values below ~0.00304 come back scaled by ~1.00023. The module doc admits clamping 'where a pixel is filled'; it does not say that unpainted pixels inside the bounds are rewritten. Tests check undo identity and 8-bit frames only, so nothing catches it. The tolerance reading (8-bit display levels, as the magic wand) and the dither reading (deterministic, at most 0.5/255, colour only) hold as declared Studio readings.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: keep the before bytes where paint alpha x opacity is 0; decode with Prism's inverse of its own encode; test an HDR value
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080 (export): coverage.map_or(u16::MAX, ...) for selection None; decode() IEC constants vs DisplayEncoding::Srgb => moncurve_r(v.clamp(0,1), 2.4, 0.055); rs = ((g-1)/o)^(g-1) * ((1+o)/g)^g = 12.923

findings_not_failures.finding: The export-sequence CLI cannot export any sequence that holds an audio clip. execute_export_sequence binds --media files to the program monitor (bind_program_media) but never calls set_export_audio, so export_prepare refuses audio_sources_missing for every sequence with an enabled audio clip. The refusal is typed and nothing is exported silent, as the lead's reading says. But the manual entry (harness-core manual.rs) says the command 'mixes the sound', and neither the lane's gaps nor the manual say the CLI is video-only. The CLI tests use a video-only package, so the limit is never shown.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: bind --media audio as the export sound port, or say video-only in the manual and add a CLI audio_sources_missing test
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080: the function calls viewer.open, bind_program_media, export_sequence; no set_export_audio; manual summary '... renders the frames, mixes the sound and encodes ...'

findings_not_failures.finding: The exported sound of a sequence does not match what the mixer plays when the parent sequence has clip gain or pan envelopes, track or master automation, bus routes, sends or effects. timeline_export.rs builds the root mix with the plain TimelineMixStream::new, in both the nested and the un-nested branch; only nested clips get their envelopes (NestedAudioSources::with_routing). NEST-2 declared this in its lane notes ('root mix stays TimelineMixStream::new (no root envelopes or bus routing, as before this lane)'). SEQ-EXPORT-UI-1 makes the path reachable from the window and the CLI for the first time, and its module docs, the form and the manual entry do not say it. A user who sets a clip pan (SMB-AU-MULTITRACK-3) or a master volume lane hears it in the mixer and does not get it in the file. Nothing refuses or labels it.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: route the export through the bus stream the mixer plays, or refuse/label an export whose root has envelopes or routing
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080; builders/lanes/hsk-studio-pr-nest-2.json notes ('export with a NestedDocument: root mix stays TimelineMixStream::new ...')

findings_not_failures.finding: SVG marker import drops the marker's own paint without a loss. recognise_marker reads only whether the marker child is filled or stroked (painted(&props, 'fill'), painted(&props, 'stroke')). It never compares the child's fill colour or opacity with the line's stroke, and it ignores a stroke on a filled child (sw = 0.0 when filled). A red arrowhead on a black line therefore imports as an arrow.triangle marker drawn in the line's colour, with no loss note. Every other unmapped marker feature in this function returns None, which keeps the typed unsupported_marker loss.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: map only when the child's paint is absent, context-stroke or equal to the stroke and unstroked; else unsupported_marker
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080: let filled = painted(&props, "fill", true); let stroked = painted(&props, "stroke", false); let sw = if hollow { ... } else { 0.0 }

findings_not_failures.finding: The .fig frame PDF export paints a marked stroke twice where marker and stroke overlap. It strokes the Nib-trimmed path, then fills each marker outline in a separate call with the same ink and alpha state. At opacity below 100 % the overlap comes out darker; composite unions stroke and markers into one plane, so the canvas and the export differ. The export test uses an opaque TRIANGLE_FILLED cap only. (The reviewer also reports the same pattern in harness-view pdf_export.rs:160; NOT_INSPECTED by the validator.)
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: fill the stroke outline united with the marker outlines as one path, or use a transparency group; add a 50 % opacity test
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080: self.ex.stroke_path(self.page, stroked, ink, style) then for (outline, rule) in &outlines { self.ex.fill_path(self.page, outline, *rule, ink) }

findings_not_failures.finding: The plain reflow entry points now lay out an auto-sized frame without saying so. reflow_core returns reflow_sized(...).map(|(p, s, _)| (p, s)) and drops the FrameResize list. reflow, reflow_typeset, reflow_flow, reflow_grid and reflow_cjk therefore place lines in a frame whose size differs from the document's, and FramePlacement carries no size. Before this lane those inputs were refused (unsupported_composition). frame_autosize.rs:243 asserts that the plain reflow equals the auto-sized layout, so this is intended. It is documented on reflow_autosize and declared in the lane notes as 'host change required'. Callers such as interop-layout's IDML reflow (which reads AutoSizingType) now get placement and overset for a size the document does not hold, with no signal.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: plain entry points keep the authored size (or refuse) when auto-size is on; only reflow_autosize resizes
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080: reflow_sized(req, opts, flow, grids, cjk, cancel).map(|(p, s, _)| (p, s)); assert_eq!(run(&doc, &st, &paras, &records()).expect("reflow"), p.layout)

findings_not_failures.finding: Nested frame expansion is not bounded by work. expand charges only media layers against max_layers. Sequence layers and the unresolved list are not charged. A valid, acyclic document in which each sequence nests the next on k tracks visits k^depth layers (up to 64 sequences), and only the cancel token stops it, so the program monitor can hang. Cycles are guarded (the stack) and resident memory is bounded. This is the same class as F-R43-3 (work walked before the budget).
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: charge every Sequence-layer expansion and every unresolved push against max_layers or a separate visit budget; add a fan-out test
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080 (unchanged since bdc15f15): the max_layers check sits inside the non-Sequence arm only; the Sequence arm recurses and out.unresolved.push is unbounded

findings_not_failures.finding: Markers on closed paths are stored and then dropped without a note. Nib reports closed and consumed subpaths. Composite's adapter keeps only o.trimmed and o.markers and discards that report, so a marker entry on a closed path renders as a plain stroke, and a fully trimmed subpath vanishes. The ARROWHEADS-1 brief asks for this case to be 'reported, not silent', which holds only inside Nib. ARROWHEADS-2's SVG import marks polygon and closed path elements as markable, so their markers import with no loss and never render. SVG viewers do draw markers on closed paths.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: surface closed/consumed subpaths as a typed per-layer note; give polygon and closed paths unsupported_marker on import
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080: trimmed.push(o.trimmed); markers.extend(o.markers ...) with no use of o.closed_subpaths / o.consumed_subpaths; matches!(.., "path" | "line" | "polyline" | "polygon")

findings_not_failures.finding: GRID work is budgeted per placement call, not per solve. place() starts its own counter (let mut ops = 0, grid.rs:194; GRID_CELL_BUDGET 1 << 24). solve calls base_size per child for both axes (grid.rs:379/384, 451/456), so nested hugging grids repeat placements. The reviewer estimates about 2^depth repeats; max_depth 32 and the cancel token are the only overall bounds. Separately, interop-fig-native maps a Figma GRID frame to LayoutMode::Grid with grid: None (native.rs:1477, :1520), so the whole .fig import is refused MissingField /auto_layout/grid (before this lane: UnsupportedDescriptor). The importer mapping is out of scope and declared in the lane notes. The two pins of other lanes moved from UnsupportedDescriptor to MissingField; that is a necessary consequence of GRID becoming storable, not a loosening.
findings_not_failures.repair_direction: share the cell budget across one solve in Ctx (or memoise content_size); importer records a typed loss for GRID until mapped
findings_not_failures.evidence: read at ff4ca080; git diff ae6452c4 ff4ca080 -- folio tests/design_records_contract.rs, components tests/auto_layout.rs
